contracts.admission: RoutineInputAdmission owns private input/size slots. Its private constructor computes size from the exact original reference/native value. prepare recognizes only the genuine ECMAScript private brand, otherwise measures raw input, and returns null for oversized input. Route, runner and ledger pass this branded value in the existing input slot. No independent receipt/raw-input pair exists; ledger unwrap reads the private slot rather than an overridable getter. Repeated prepare calls reuse the captured measurement, not a global cache. Native stringify/byteLength errors escape at their original locations; route handles the null oversize result outside its existing try, preserving JSON 413 versus native rejection ownership.
contracts.parentApproval: Parent explicitly approved revised existing-input-slot private-brand contract before admission implementation: captured measurement, NOT immutable snapshot; preserve original reference/native value; one size/toJSON validation replaces three; persistence/prompt serialization remain; keep all three ingress error orderings; no unchecked ledger operation.
contracts.deliberateDifference: Mutable input and stateful toJSON are observed once for admission. Captured measurement does not constrain later mutations or later persistence/response serialization, and never claims the persisted representation is an immutable <=32KiB snapshot. No JSON normalization or deep freeze. Normal HTTP ingress is parsed JSON; the explicit native JavaScript regression demonstrates first-validation behavior without normalization.
contracts.serializationAccounting: Baseline measured 3 compact root-input size serializations per accepted HTTP invocation; final measures 1. Final explicit toJSON probe observes 3 original-object calls when including initial containing-ledger persistence and response JSON serialization: size + persistence + response. Prompt composition remains a later serialization of reread persisted input. This is not a claim that every serialization/toJSON executes once.
